subject: EastUS1: sudden throughput & latency surge — request for priority backstop

We're seeing a sharp rise in p99 latency and 5xx rates out of eastus1 starting ~13:40 PDT. Throughput for our production key dropped ~60%. Errors are predominantly 502/504s. Attached a short log extract. This is impacting our checkout flow — customers are timing out. Can your ops team confirm whether this is an ongoing regional issue and advise on a fast fallback?

We need an estimate on timeframe to recover or to move traffic to eastus2.

-Tom

- Dylan will run a fast health sweep + KV cache pressure check in eastus1 and surface whether it's localized to a subset of hosts.
- If the region is unstable we will initiate a controlled cross-region steer to eastus2 (can be done within ~15–30 minutes) and keep a subset pinned to eastus1 for verification.

Tom — will update in 10.

Rachel

Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 14:18:51 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike in eastus1 (impacts inference requests)

Quick technical update (internal notes included inline):

- Observed: eastus1 telemetry shows a cluster of throttled workers in AZ-a (node pool az-a-*) with rising GC and large KV-cache misses. P99 token latency jumped from ~80ms to ~1.2s around 13:35. Error burst correlates with degraded gRPC connections to a subset of RL worker shards.
- Likely cause: localized kernel driver mismatch + transient network queueing on AZ-a's ToR (we're seeing packet retransmits).

Recommended immediate steps:
1) Trigger a regional partial-steer of 65% of AcmeTech's traffic to eastus2 (safe-config: sticky sessions preserved for 35% to validate state).
2) Warm a compatible eastus2 pool with same quantization profile and model variant (we have spare capacity; warm up ETA ~8–12 minutes).
3) Apply KV-cache priming for their top 200 prefixes to avoid cold-start amplification after steer.

I've attached a draft runbook for the partial-steer: eastus1-runbook-draft.md. Ops: please review for throttling thresholds.

I'll execute the health sweep now and post back with immediate go/no-go.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks | Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Production latency spike in eastus1 (impacts inference requests)

Thanks — I reviewed the telemetry. If Dylan validates the ToR retransmit pattern, we should proceed with the partial-steer. A couple of notes for authorization and exec comms:

- We can enable AcmeTech as 'priority backstop' in our routing for this incident. That gives them reserved capacity on the eastus2 warm pool and higher retry budget. This requires Ops approval for usage-based priority and a short-term billing exception.
- Proposed commercial remediation: offer a one-time 25% credit on their monthly usage for the affected window (we've used this band in prior incidents). Vanessa, please draft the customer-facing credit authorization and I'll sign off.

If leadership needs to be looped, please include the following brief: one-line impact, estimated diversion minutes, and credit ask ($estimate attached in the hubspot link).

Marcus Lin | Head of Production Ops, Redwood Inference

Tom — update and next steps:

- We initiated a controlled partial-steer at 15:05 PDT. ~68% of your traffic is now routed to eastus2; 32% remains pinned to eastus1 for verification. Early metrics show 5xx rate down ~85% for steered traffic and end-to-end P95 latency reduced to ~120ms.
- We warmed an eastus2 pool with the same model variant and primed KV caches for your top prefixes; this reduced cold-start amplification.
- Marcus has approved a one-time remediation credit; Vanessa will send the formal credit authorization and a short incident summary within the hour.

Next ask for AcmeTech platform team: please validate session consistency on your side for traffic routed to eastus2 and share any anomalies. We'll keep eastus1 pinned for 30 minutes of stable telemetry, then either restore or maintain the steer based on results.

We attached the runbook link and a latency snapshot for your team. Reaching out to your SRE for a quick sync if needed.

Apologies again — we'll follow up with a full post-incident report within 72 hours.

Warmly,
Rachel Kim | Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
